questions.questionText: Which of the following is a balanced chemical equation for the reaction of hydrogen with oxygen to form water?
questions.hint: Count atoms on both sides.
questions.explanation: Balanced equation has equal atoms on both sides. Option B satisfies this.

questions.questionText: The reaction: 2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂ is an example of:
questions.hint: Check oxidation and reduction.
questions.explanation: PbO is reduced to Pb and C is oxidized to CO₂, so it is a redox reaction.

questions.questionText: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler substances is called:
questions.hint: Breakdown of compound.
questions.explanation: Decomposition reaction involves breaking down into simpler substances.

questions.questionText: When iron nails are placed in copper sulphate solution, the colour changes from blue to:
questions.hint: FeSO₄ formation.
questions.explanation: Iron displaces copper forming FeSO₄ solution which is green.

questions.questionText: Which is a double displacement reaction?
questions.hint: Exchange of ions.
questions.explanation: NaOH and HCl exchange ions to form NaCl and H₂O.

questions.questionText: Which of the following reactions is a combination reaction?
questions.hint: Two reactants combine to form one product.
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide combines with water to form calcium hydroxide.

questions.questionText: What happens when magnesium ribbon is burnt in air?
questions.optionB: It burns with dazzling white flame
questions.hint: Recall laboratory activity.
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame forming magnesium oxide.

questions.questionText: Which gas is evolved when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.hint: Metal + acid reaction.
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Hydrogen gas is released.

questions.questionText: The insoluble substance formed in a precipitation reaction is called:
questions.hint: Solid formed in solution.
questions.explanation: An insoluble solid formed during reaction is called precipitate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents oxidation?
questions.hint: Definition of oxidation.
questions.explanation: Oxidation is addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen.

questions.questionText: The reaction in which heat is absorbed is called:
questions.hint: Heat absorbed.
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb heat.

questions.questionText: Rancidity can be prevented by:
questions.hint: Prevent oxidation.
questions.explanation: Antioxidants prevent oxidation of fats and oils.

questions.questionText: Which is a thermal decomposition reaction?
questions.hint: Heat causes breakdown.
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating.

questions.questionText: In the reaction MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂, which substance is oxidized?
questions.hint: Oxidation involves loss of electrons.
questions.explanation: Chloride ions from HCl lose electrons to form chlorine gas.

questions.questionText: Copper powder turns black on heating because:
questions.hint: Black coating forms.
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with oxygen to form black copper oxide.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an exothermic process?
questions.hint: Energy released.
questions.explanation: Respiration releases energy in the form of heat.

questions.questionText: What type of reaction is represented by AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃?
questions.hint: Exchange of ions occurs.
questions.explanation: The ions exchange partners forming AgCl precipitate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is reduced in the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O?
questions.hint: Reduction means removal of oxygen.
questions.explanation: CuO loses oxygen to form copper, hence it is reduced.

questions.questionText: Food packets are flushed with nitrogen gas to:
questions.hint: Nitrogen prevents oxidation.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen prevents oxidation of oils and fats.

questions.questionText: Which reaction occurs when electricity is passed through acidified water?
questions.hint: Decomposition by electricity.
questions.explanation: Electric current decomposes water into hydrogen and oxygen.

tests.title: Chemical Reactions – Test 3 (Corrosion, Oxidation States & Analysis)

questions.questionText: The green coating that appears on copper vessels over time is due to:
questions.hint: Corrosion of copper in moist air with CO₂.
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with CO₂ and moisture to form basic copper carbonate (Cu(OH)₂·CuCO₃), which is green.

questions.questionText: What is the oxidation state of manganese in MnO₂?
questions.hint: Oxygen has -2 oxidation state.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a physical change?
questions.hint: A new substance is formed.
questions.explanation: Rusting involves a chemical reaction forming iron oxide — a new substance — so it is a chemical change.

questions.questionText: In the reaction 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, what type of reaction is this?
questions.hint: One reactant breaks into simpler products.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen — a classic decomposition reaction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines a reducing agent?
questions.optionB: A substance that loses electrons and gets oxidized
questions.optionC: A substance that causes reduction in another and itself gets oxidized
questions.hint: Think about what the reducing agent does to the other reactant.
questions.explanation: A reducing agent reduces another substance and is itself oxidized in the process.

questions.questionText: Silver articles turn black over time due to formation of:
questions.hint: Reaction with sulphur compounds in air.
questions.explanation: Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) in air to form black silver sulphide (Ag₂S).

questions.questionText: Photosynthesis can be represented as: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. This is an example of:
questions.hint: Energy is absorbed; oxidation states also change.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs light energy (endothermic) and involves oxidation of water and reduction of CO₂ (redox).

questions.questionText: When sodium hydroxide reacts with hydrochloric acid, the reaction is:
questions.hint: Acid + base reaction.
questions.explanation: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O is a neutralisation reaction, which is a type of double displacement.

questions.questionText: Which condition is required for the decomposition of silver chloride?
questions.hint: Used in black-and-white photography.
questions.explanation: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ occurs in sunlight. This photolytic decomposition is used in photography.

questions.questionText: In the thermite reaction: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe, which substance acts as the oxidising agent?
questions.hint: Which substance causes oxidation of the other?
questions.explanation: Fe₂O₃ oxidises Al (Al gets oxidised to Al₂O₃) and is itself reduced to Fe. So Fe₂O₃ is the oxidising agent.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs shows both a combination and an exothermic reaction?
questions.hint: Haber process — industrial synthesis of ammonia.
questions.explanation: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ is a combination reaction (two reactants → one product) and releases heat (exothermic).

questions.questionText: A student adds dilute H₂SO₄ to zinc granules. Which observation confirms the reaction is a displacement?
questions.optionC: Evolution of a colourless gas that burns with a pop sound
questions.hint: Zn displaces H from H₂SO₄.
questions.explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑. H₂ gas is colourless and burns with a pop sound — confirming displacement of hydrogen by zinc.

questions.questionText: During electrolysis of water, the ratio of volume of hydrogen to oxygen collected at electrodes is:
questions.hint: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂
questions.explanation: From the balanced equation, 2 moles of H₂ are produced for every 1 mole of O₂, giving a 2:1 volume ratio.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about a balanced chemical equation?
questions.optionA: Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
questions.optionB: Number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides
questions.optionC: Number of molecules is always equal on both sides
questions.optionD: It obeys the law of conservation of mass
questions.hint: Atoms are conserved, but molecules may not be.
questions.explanation: Balancing conserves atoms and mass, not necessarily the number of molecules. E.g. 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has 3 molecules on left and 2 on right.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): When a strip of copper is placed in silver nitrate solution, the solution turns blue.
Reason (R): Copper displaces silver from silver nitrate solution and copper nitrate is formed.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.optionC: A is true but R is false
questions.optionD: A is false but R is true
questions.hint: Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag
questions.explanation: Copper displaces silver; the blue colour is due to Cu(NO₃)₂ in solution. Both A and R are correct and causally linked.

questions.questionText: Quicklime (CaO) reacts with water vigorously and releases heat. This reaction is best classified as:
questions.hint: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + heat
questions.explanation: CaO and H₂O combine to form one product Ca(OH)₂ (combination) and heat is released (exothermic).

questions.questionText: Which of the following best explains why chips manufacturers flush bags with nitrogen gas?
questions.optionC: Nitrogen is inert and prevents oxidation of fats in chips
questions.optionD: Nitrogen increases shelf life by killing bacteria
questions.hint: Rancidity prevention.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is chemically inert. It displaces oxygen in the packet, preventing oxidation of oils/fats and hence preventing rancidity.

questions.questionText: The reaction between barium chloride and sodium sulphate produces a white precipitate of barium sulphate. This is an example of:
questions.hint: Both ions exchange partners; insoluble product forms.
questions.explanation: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ + 2NaCl. Ions exchange (double displacement) and BaSO₄ precipitates out of solution.

questions.questionText: Which change in oxidation number correctly identifies the reducing agent in: H₂ + CuO → Cu + H₂O?
questions.optionA: Cu changes from +2 to 0; Cu is the reducing agent
questions.optionB: H changes from 0 to +1; H₂ is the reducing agent
questions.optionC: O changes from -2 to 0; CuO is the reducing agent
questions.optionD: H changes from +1 to 0; H₂O is the reducing agent
questions.hint: Reducing agent gets oxidised — its oxidation number increases.
questions.explanation: H in H₂ goes from 0 to +1 (oxidised). H₂ loses electrons, causing reduction of CuO, so H₂ is the reducing agent.

questions.questionText: A precipitate of lead iodide (yellow) is formed when lead nitrate solution is mixed with potassium iodide solution. Which type of reaction is this?
questions.hint: Pb²⁺ and I⁻ exchange from their respective compounds.
questions.explanation: Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂↓ + 2KNO₃. The cations and anions exchange partners — a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.

tests.title: Acids, Bases and Salts – Test 1 (Basics & Indicators)

questions.questionText: Which of the following turns blue litmus red?
questions.hint: Acids turn blue litmus red.
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is acidic in nature and turns blue litmus red.

questions.questionText: The pH value of a neutral solution is:
questions.hint: Neutral solutions have equal H⁺ and OH⁻ ions.
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral and has pH 7.

questions.questionText: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid?
questions.hint: Metal + acid reaction.
questions.explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Hydrogen gas is evolved.

questions.questionText: Phenolphthalein indicator turns pink in:
questions.hint: Phenolphthalein works in bases.
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acids and pink in bases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a natural indicator?
questions.hint: Obtained from lichens.
questions.explanation: Litmus is a natural indicator extracted from lichens.

questions.questionText: Acids in aqueous solution produce:
questions.hint: Characteristic ion of acids.
questions.explanation: Acids release hydrogen ions in water.

questions.questionText: Which acid is present in lemon juice?
questions.hint: Found in citrus fruits.
questions.explanation: Citric acid is naturally present in lemon and orange.

questions.questionText: What is the nature of sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.hint: NaOH is a base.
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide releases OH⁻ ions in water.

questions.questionText: Turmeric indicator changes to reddish-brown in:
questions.hint: Turmeric reacts with bases.
questions.explanation: Turmeric turns reddish-brown in basic solutions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following substances is used in antacids?
questions.hint: Neutralises excess stomach acid.
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a mild base used in antacids.

tests.title: Acids, Bases and Salts – Test 2 (pH & Reactions)

questions.questionText: Which of the following has the highest pH?
questions.hint: Higher pH means more basic.
questions.explanation: Soap solution is basic and has high pH.

questions.questionText: The reaction between an acid and a base is called:
questions.hint: Acid + base → salt + water.
questions.explanation: Neutralisation forms salt and water.

questions.questionText: Which acid is present in vinegar?
questions.hint: Common kitchen acid.
questions.explanation: Vinegar contains dilute acetic acid.

questions.questionText: What effect does a basic solution have on red and blue litmus?
questions.optionA: Turns red litmus blue; blue litmus remains unchanged
questions.optionB: Turns blue litmus red; red litmus remains unchanged
questions.optionC: Turns both red and blue litmus green
questions.optionD: No effect on either red or blue litmus
questions.hint: Bases affect only red litmus.
questions.explanation: Basic solutions turn red litmus blue. Blue litmus is already blue and remains unchanged in a basic solution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following salts is used in baking powder?
questions.hint: NaHCO₃.
questions.explanation: Baking powder contains baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃) as its key ingredient, which releases CO₂ when heated.

questions.questionText: The gas evolved when baking soda reacts with acid is:
questions.hint: Makes cakes fluffy.
questions.explanation: CO₂ gas is released during the reaction.

questions.questionText: Tooth decay starts when pH of mouth is below:
questions.hint: Acidic conditions damage enamel.
questions.explanation: Below pH 5.5 enamel starts corroding.

questions.questionText: Which substance is used for making bleaching powder?
questions.hint: Slaked lime.
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is produced using calcium hydroxide: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.hint: Completely ionises in water.
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is a strong mineral acid.

questions.questionText: The common name of calcium sulphate hemihydrate is:
questions.hint: Used for casts.
questions.explanation: CaSO₄·½H₂O is called Plaster of Paris.

tests.title: Acids, Bases and Salts – Test 3 (Salts, Water of Crystallisation & Applications)

questions.questionText: The chemical formula of washing soda is:
questions.hint: Sodium carbonate decahydrate.
questions.explanation: Washing soda is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O — sodium carbonate with 10 molecules of water of crystallisation.

questions.questionText: What is the water of crystallisation in blue vitriol (copper sulphate)?
questions.hint: CuSO₄·?H₂O
questions.explanation: Blue vitriol is CuSO₄·5H₂O — it has 5 molecules of water of crystallisation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is used as a disinfectant in municipal water supply?
questions.hint: Chlorine-releasing compound.
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂) releases chlorine which disinfects water.

questions.questionText: Plaster of Paris hardens when mixed with water because:
questions.optionB: It absorbs water to form a hard crystalline structure
questions.optionD: It reacts with CO₂ in air
questions.hint: Reverse of dehydration.
questions.explanation: CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O (gypsum). It rehydrates to form a hard set structure.

questions.questionText: Which salt has basic nature?
questions.hint: Formed from strong base + weak acid.
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ is formed from strong base (NaOH) and weak acid (H₂CO₃), so it is a basic salt with pH > 7.

questions.questionText: Sodium hydrogen carbonate is heated. Which gas is released?
questions.hint: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + ?
questions.explanation: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. CO₂ is released on heating.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes is used to obtain NaOH on a large scale?
questions.hint: Electrolysis of brine.
questions.explanation: The chlor-alkali process involves electrolysis of brine (NaCl solution) to produce NaOH, Cl₂, and H₂.

questions.questionText: What is produced at the cathode during electrolysis of brine?
questions.hint: Reduction occurs at cathode.
questions.explanation: At the cathode: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. Hydrogen gas is released.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes a dilute acid?
questions.optionB: An acid with a high concentration of H⁺ ions
questions.optionC: An acid dissolved in a large amount of water
questions.optionD: An acid that does not ionise
questions.hint: Dilute = more water, fewer acid molecules per litre.
questions.explanation: A dilute acid has a relatively low concentration — it has been dissolved in a large amount of water.

questions.questionText: The pH of human blood is approximately:
questions.hint: Slightly basic, strictly regulated.
questions.explanation: Human blood has a pH of 7.35–7.45. Even small deviations from this range can be life-threatening.

tests.title: Acids, Bases and Salts – Test 4 (Advanced & Application)

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Dry HCl gas does not change the colour of dry litmus.
Reason (R): HCl produces H⁺ ions only in the presence of water.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.optionC: A is true but R is false
questions.optionD: A is false but R is true
questions.hint: Ionisation requires water.
questions.explanation: HCl shows acidic properties only when dissolved in water (H⁺ ions form). Dry HCl has no free H⁺ ions, so dry litmus is unaffected.

questions.questionText: A solution turns red litmus blue. When excess BaCl₂ solution is added to it, a white precipitate forms. The solution most likely contains:
questions.hint: Basic solution + carbonate ion precipitates with Ba²⁺.
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ is basic (turns red litmus blue) and CO₃²⁻ reacts with Ba²⁺ from BaCl₂ to form white BaCO₃ precipitate. The question now states 'excess BaCl₂' to make clear it is a test for carbonate, not sulphate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs of solutions, when mixed, would produce a white precipitate?
questions.hint: Insoluble sulphate forms.
questions.explanation: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄↓ (white precipitate) + 2NaCl. Barium sulphate is insoluble.

questions.questionText: A farmer finds his soil is too acidic for crops. Which of the following should he add?
questions.hint: Neutralise acidity.
questions.explanation: Slaked lime (Ca(OH)₂) is a base that neutralises excess acidity in soil, raising its pH.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about the chlor-alkali process is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: Chlorine is produced at the anode
questions.optionB: Hydrogen is produced at the cathode
questions.optionC: NaOH is formed near the cathode
questions.optionD: The solution used is dilute HCl
questions.hint: Which solution is electrolysed?
questions.explanation: The chlor-alkali process uses brine (NaCl solution), not HCl. Electrolysis gives Cl₂ at anode, H₂ at cathode, and NaOH in solution.

questions.questionText: When copper sulphate crystals are heated, they turn white because:
questions.hint: CuSO₄·5H₂O → CuSO₄ + ?
questions.explanation: On heating, CuSO₄·5H₂O loses its 5 water molecules to form anhydrous CuSO₄, which is white.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly explains why concentrated H₂SO₄ should always be added to water and not the reverse?
questions.optionA: Water evaporates when acid is added to it
questions.optionB: The reaction is endothermic; diluting acid first is safer
questions.optionC: Mixing is highly exothermic; adding acid to water dissipates heat safely
questions.optionD: Acid reacts with glass if water is added first
questions.hint: Think about heat generation and safety.
questions.explanation: Dissolving H₂SO₄ in water is highly exothermic. Adding acid to water (large volume) dissipates heat safely. Adding water to acid causes the small water volume to boil violently and splatter acid.

questions.questionText: A solution has a pH of 3. If it is diluted 10 times, its new pH will approximately be:
questions.hint: Dilution reduces H⁺ concentration by 10×.
questions.explanation: pH = –log[H⁺]. At pH 3, [H⁺] = 10⁻³. Diluting 10× gives [H⁺] = 10⁻⁴, so pH = 4.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can act as both an acid and a base depending on the reaction?
questions.hint: It can donate or accept H⁺.
questions.explanation: Water is amphoteric — it donates H⁺ to a stronger base (acting as acid) and accepts H⁺ from a stronger acid (acting as base). [Note: This concept goes slightly beyond standard NCERT Class 10 but appears in CBSE competency-based questions.]

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): NH₄Cl solution is acidic in nature.
Reason (R): NH₄Cl is formed from a weak base (NH₄OH) and a strong acid (HCl).
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.optionC: A is true but R is false
questions.optionD: A is false but R is true
questions.hint: Salt of weak base + strong acid is acidic.
questions.explanation: Salts of weak bases and strong acids hydrolyse to give acidic solutions. NH₄Cl dissociates and NH₄⁺ reacts with water releasing H⁺ ions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic property of most metals?
questions.hint: Recall the physical properties of metals.
questions.explanation: Most metals are malleable, meaning they can be beaten into thin sheets. They are also good conductors of heat and electricity. Brittle substances usually break on hammering.

questions.questionText: Which gas is generally produced when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.hint: Think about the general reaction of metals with dilute acids.
questions.explanation: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid according to the equation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Therefore, hydrogen gas is evolved.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals is stored in kerosene to prevent its reaction with air and moisture?
questions.hint: Think about highly reactive alkali metals.
questions.explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and reacts rapidly with oxygen and moisture. Hence, it is stored under kerosene to prevent accidental reactions.

questions.questionText: Which oxide is amphoteric in nature?
questions.hint: Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases.
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric. Sodium oxide, magnesium oxide and calcium oxide are basic oxides.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct regarding ionic compounds?
questions.optionA: They generally conduct electricity in the solid state.
questions.optionB: They usually have low melting points.
questions.optionC: They conduct electricity in molten or aqueous state due to free ions.
questions.hint: Think about the movement of ions.
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds conduct electricity only when their ions are free to move, such as in the molten or aqueous state. In the solid state, ions remain fixed in position.

questions.questionText: A brown metal develops a green coating after long exposure to moist air. The coating mainly consists of:
questions.hint: Recall the green layer formed on copper utensils.
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with oxygen, carbon dioxide and moisture to form a green coating of basic copper carbonate, CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂.

questions.questionText: Why are sulphide ores generally roasted before reduction?
questions.optionA: To convert sulphides into oxides, which are easier to reduce
questions.optionB: To remove all impurities by melting
questions.optionC: To increase the weight of the ore
questions.hint: Think about the first step in extracting metals from sulphide ores.
questions.explanation: Roasting involves heating sulphide ores in the presence of oxygen. This converts sulphides into oxides, which can then be reduced more easily to obtain the metal.

questions.questionText: Which method is commonly used to prevent rusting of iron by coating it with zinc?
questions.hint: A protective zinc layer prevents rusting.
questions.explanation: Galvanization is the process of coating iron with zinc. The zinc layer protects iron from contact with air and moisture, thereby preventing rusting.

questions.questionText: Iron, zinc, silver and copper strips are placed separately in copper sulphate solution. Which metals will displace copper from the solution?
questions.hint: Use the reactivity series.
questions.explanation: Iron and zinc are more reactive than copper, so they displace copper from copper sulphate solution. Silver is less reactive than copper, and copper cannot displace itself.

questions.questionText: Four metals P, Q, R and S are arranged in decreasing order of reactivity as P > Q > R > S. If P reacts vigorously with cold water, which statement must be true?
questions.optionA: S can displace P from its salt solution.
questions.optionB: R can displace Q from its salt solution.
questions.optionC: P can displace Q, R and S from their salt solutions.
questions.optionD: Q is less reactive than S.
questions.hint: Apply the given reactivity order carefully.
questions.explanation: Since P is the most reactive metal among the four, it can displace all the less reactive metals (Q, R and S) from their respective salt solutions. The other statements contradict the given reactivity order.

questions.questionText: Which of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.hint: Think of the allotropes of carbon.
questions.explanation: Graphite is an allotrope of carbon that conducts electricity because it has free electrons between its layers. Most other non-metals are poor conductors.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals is liquid at room temperature?
questions.hint: Only one common metal remains liquid under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only common metal that exists in the liquid state at room temperature.

questions.questionText: What is formed when magnesium burns in air?
questions.hint: Magnesium reacts with oxygen.
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame in oxygen to form magnesium oxide. The reaction is: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals cannot be extracted by reducing its oxide with carbon?
questions.hint: Refer to the reactivity series.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon. Therefore, its oxide cannot be reduced by carbon and is extracted by electrolytic reduction.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct about metal oxides?
questions.optionB: Most metal oxides are basic in nature.
questions.optionD: All metal oxides dissolve in water.
questions.hint: Recall the general nature of metal oxides.
questions.explanation: Most metal oxides are basic because they react with acids to form salt and water. Some metal oxides such as aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are amphoteric.

questions.questionText: An element X reacts with oxygen to form an acidic oxide. X is most likely a:
questions.hint: Think about the nature of non-metal oxides.
questions.explanation: Non-metals generally form acidic oxides. For example, sulphur forms sulphur dioxide, which is acidic in nature.

questions.questionText: Which process is used to obtain highly reactive metals such as sodium and calcium from their molten compounds?
questions.hint: Highly reactive metals require electricity for extraction.
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals such as sodium and calcium are extracted by electrolysis of their molten salts because chemical reduction is not feasible.

questions.questionText: Which of the following observations indicates that a displacement reaction has occurred when an iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution?
questions.optionA: The blue solution becomes green and a reddish-brown coating forms on the nail.
questions.optionB: The solution becomes colourless with no deposit.
questions.hint: Recall the reaction between iron and copper sulphate.
questions.explanation: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution. The blue solution turns green due to iron sulphate formation, and copper is deposited as a reddish-brown coating.

questions.questionText: A metal X displaces zinc from zinc sulphate solution. Which statement is definitely true?
questions.optionA: X is less reactive than zinc.
questions.optionB: X is more reactive than zinc.
questions.optionD: X cannot react with dilute acids.
questions.hint: Apply the displacement rule.
questions.explanation: Only a metal more reactive than zinc can displace zinc from its salt solution. Therefore, X must be more reactive than zinc.

questions.questionText: Four metals A, B, C and D are arranged in increasing order of reactivity as D < C < B < A. If C does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid but B reacts vigorously, which conclusion is correct?
questions.optionA: D will react vigorously with dilute hydrochloric acid.
questions.optionB: A is more reactive than B and can displace C and D from their salt solutions.
questions.optionC: C is more reactive than B.
questions.optionD: B cannot displace C from its salt solution.
questions.hint: Use both the reactivity order and displacement rule.
questions.explanation: Since A is the most reactive metal, it can displace B, C and D from their salt solutions. As B is more reactive than C, it can also displace C. Hence, option B is correct.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals can be cut easily with a knife?
questions.hint: Think about very soft alkali metals.
questions.explanation: Sodium is a soft alkali metal and can be easily cut with a knife. Most other metals are comparatively hard.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a non-metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature?
questions.hint: Only one common non-metal is liquid at room temperature.
questions.explanation: Bromine is the only common non-metal that exists as a reddish-brown liquid at room temperature.

questions.questionText: Which of the following reactions is an example of a displacement reaction?
questions.hint: One metal replaces another from its salt solution.
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces it from copper sulphate solution. This is a displacement reaction.

questions.questionText: Which property makes aluminium suitable for making cooking utensils?
questions.optionC: Good conductor of heat and resistant to corrosion
questions.hint: Consider both heat conduction and durability.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a good conductor of heat and forms a protective oxide layer that prevents corrosion, making it suitable for cooking utensils.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.hint: Look at the position of the metal relative to hydrogen in the reactivity series.
questions.explanation: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen and therefore does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid. Magnesium, zinc and iron react to produce hydrogen gas.

questions.questionText: Why are ionic compounds generally brittle?
questions.optionB: Layers of ions shift under force, bringing like charges together which repel each other.
questions.optionC: They have very low melting points.
questions.optionD: They are made of neutral atoms only.
questions.hint: Think about the arrangement of ions in a crystal lattice.
questions.explanation: When force is applied, the layers of ions shift, causing like charges to come close together. The strong repulsion between like charges breaks the crystal, making ionic compounds brittle.

questions.questionText: Which process is used to concentrate sulphide ores before extraction of metals?
questions.hint: This method makes use of differences in surface properties.
questions.explanation: Froth flotation is commonly used to concentrate sulphide ores. The sulphide particles attach to the froth and are separated from impurities.

questions.questionText: An iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution for some time. Which of the following changes is expected?
questions.optionA: Blue solution becomes green and copper is deposited on the nail.
questions.optionB: Green solution becomes blue and iron is deposited.
questions.optionC: No change occurs because iron is less reactive than copper.
questions.hint: Use the reactivity series.
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper. It displaces copper from copper sulphate solution, producing iron sulphate (green solution) and depositing copper on the nail.

questions.questionText: Four metals W, X, Y and Z are arranged in decreasing order of reactivity as W > X > Y > Z. Which pair of reactions is possible?
questions.optionA: Y displaces X from XSO₄ and Z displaces W from WSO₄.
questions.optionB: X displaces Y from YSO₄ and W displaces Z from ZSO₄.
questions.optionC: Z displaces Y from YSO₄ and Y displaces X from XSO₄.
questions.optionD: Y displaces W from WSO₄ and X displaces W from WSO₄.
questions.hint: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal.
questions.explanation: Since W > X > Y > Z, X can displace Y and W can displace Z from their salt solutions. The other options involve a less reactive metal trying to displace a more reactive one.

questions.questionText: A student performs four experiments: (I) Sodium with cold water, (II) Iron with steam, (III) Copper with dilute HCl, (IV) Zinc with dilute H2SO4. Which combination correctly represents the experiments in which hydrogen gas is evolved?
questions.hint: Recall reactions of metals with water and dilute acids.
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts with cold water to produce hydrogen. Iron reacts with steam to produce hydrogen. Zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to produce hydrogen. Copper does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid because it is less reactive than hydrogen. Therefore, experiments I, II and IV evolve hydrogen gas.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals is used for making electrical wires mainly because of its high electrical conductivity and ductility?
questions.hint: Think of the metal commonly used in household wiring.
questions.explanation: Copper is highly ductile and an excellent conductor of electricity, making it suitable for electrical wiring.

questions.questionText: Which of the following non-metals is essential for respiration in living organisms?
questions.hint: It supports breathing and combustion.
questions.explanation: Oxygen is essential for respiration and is required by most living organisms to release energy from food.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Zinc can displace copper from copper sulphate solution. Reason (R): Zinc is more reactive than copper.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Use the reactivity series.
questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the reactivity series. Therefore, zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate solution. The reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Ionic compounds conduct electricity in the solid state. Reason (R): Ions are free to move in the solid state.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is false, but R is true.
questions.optionD: Both A and R are false.
questions.hint: Think about the movement of ions in solids.
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds do not conduct electricity in the solid state because their ions are fixed in a rigid crystal lattice and cannot move. Therefore, both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.questionText: Which process is used to remove volatile impurities from a metal by heating it strongly in the absence of air?
questions.hint: It is commonly used for carbonate and hydrated ores.
questions.explanation: Calcination involves heating an ore in the absence or limited supply of air to remove volatile substances such as water and carbon dioxide.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis. Reason (R): Aluminium is more reactive than carbon.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Consider the position of aluminium in the reactivity series.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce aluminium oxide. Hence, aluminium is extracted by electrolytic reduction. The reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: A metal oxide reacts with both hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution. The oxide is most likely:
questions.hint: Look for an amphoteric oxide.
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide is amphoteric. It reacts with both acids and bases, unlike the other basic oxides listed.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Rusting of iron is a chemical change. Reason (R): Rusting results in the formation of a new substance called hydrated iron(III) oxide.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Think about the definition of a chemical change.
questions.explanation: Rusting produces hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is a new substance. Therefore, rusting is a chemical change, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Four metals A, B, C and D are arranged in the order A > B > C > D according to their reactivity. Which of the following reactions is NOT possible?
questions.hint: A less reactive metal cannot displace a more reactive one.
questions.explanation: Since A is more reactive than C, metal C cannot displace A from its salt solution. The remaining reactions are possible because a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Silver ornaments do not rust like iron. Reason (R): Rusting is a term specifically used for the corrosion of iron and its alloys.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Different metals undergo different types of corrosion.
questions.explanation: Rusting specifically refers to the corrosion of iron and its alloys. Silver undergoes tarnishing instead of rusting. Hence, both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Carbon has four electrons in its outermost shell. To attain a stable electronic configuration, carbon generally forms:
questions.optionA: Ionic bonds by losing four electrons
questions.optionB: Ionic bonds by gaining four electrons
questions.optionC: Covalent bonds by sharing four electrons
questions.hint: Think about why carbon rarely forms C4+ or C4− ions.
questions.explanation: Carbon has four valence electrons and completes its octet by sharing electrons with other atoms. Therefore, it forms covalent bonds instead of gaining or losing four electrons, which would require a very large amount of energy.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.hint: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single covalent bonds.
questions.explanation: Ethane (C₂H₆) contains only single covalent bonds and is therefore a saturated hydrocarbon. Ethene, ethyne and propene are unsaturated hydrocarbons.

questions.questionText: Which homologous series is represented by the general formula CnH2n+2?
questions.hint: Recall the general formula of saturated hydrocarbons.
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2. Alkenes have the formula CnH2n, while alkynes have CnH2n−2.

questions.questionText: Which reagent is commonly used to distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons?
questions.hint: It gets decolourised by compounds containing multiple bonds.
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water due to the addition reaction, whereas saturated hydrocarbons do not react under normal conditions.

questions.questionText: The functional group present in ethanol is:
questions.hint: Identify the characteristic group of alcohols.
questions.explanation: Ethanol is an alcohol and contains the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group.

questions.questionText: What is formed when ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid?
questions.hint: This reaction is called esterification.
questions.explanation: Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form ethyl ethanoate (an ester) and water. This is known as esterification.

questions.questionText: Which statement about soap is correct?
questions.optionA: Soap works effectively only in hard water.
questions.optionB: Soap molecules have both hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends.
questions.optionD: Soap forms scum in soft water only.
questions.hint: Think about how soap removes grease.
questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic (water-attracting) ionic end and a hydrophobic (oil-attracting) hydrocarbon end. This enables soap to form micelles and remove grease.

questions.questionText: A compound has the molecular formula C3H6. It decolourises bromine water. The compound is most likely:
questions.hint: Use the molecular formula and the bromine water test.
questions.explanation: Propene (C3H6) is an alkene containing a carbon-carbon double bond. It decolourises bromine water due to an addition reaction.

questions.questionText: During the combustion of methane in sufficient oxygen, the products formed are:
questions.hint: Think about complete combustion.
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of methane occurs according to the equation: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Therefore, carbon dioxide and water are formed.

questions.questionText: A hydrocarbon X has the molecular formula C4H8. It reacts with bromine water and forms only a single addition product. Which conclusion is correct?
questions.optionB: X is an alkene containing a carbon-carbon double bond.
questions.optionC: X belongs to the alcohol family.
questions.hint: Use both the molecular formula and the bromine water test.
questions.explanation: The formula C4H8 follows the general formula CnH2n for alkenes. Since it decolourises bromine water by addition, X must contain a carbon-carbon double bond and is therefore an alkene.

questions.questionText: Which property of carbon allows it to form a very large number of compounds?
questions.hint: Think about carbon forming long chains.
questions.explanation: Carbon exhibits catenation, which is the ability of carbon atoms to form long chains, branched chains and rings by bonding with one another. This property is responsible for the vast number of carbon compounds.

questions.questionText: The molecular formula of propane is:
questions.hint: Use the general formula of alkanes.
questions.explanation: Propane is an alkane. Alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2. For n = 3, the formula is C3H8.

questions.questionText: Which functional group is present in ethanoic acid?
questions.hint: Identify the functional group of carboxylic acids.
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid belongs to the carboxylic acid family and contains the carboxyl (-COOH) functional group.

questions.questionText: Which reaction converts an unsaturated hydrocarbon into a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.hint: Hydrogen is added across a multiple bond.
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation is the addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated hydrocarbon in the presence of a catalyst such as nickel, converting it into a saturated hydrocarbon.

questions.questionText: Which catalyst is commonly used for the hydrogenation of vegetable oils?
questions.hint: It is a finely divided transition metal.
questions.explanation: Finely divided nickel is commonly used as a catalyst during the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to produce vanaspati ghee.

questions.questionText: A compound has the molecular formula C2H4. It belongs to which homologous series?
questions.hint: Compare the formula with the general formula of hydrocarbons.
questions.explanation: C2H4 follows the general formula CnH2n, which represents alkenes. Ethene is the first stable member of this series.

questions.questionText: Why do soaps form scum in hard water?
questions.optionB: They react with calcium and magnesium ions.
questions.hint: Hard water contains certain dissolved salts.
questions.explanation: Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions, which react with soap to form insoluble precipitates called scum. This reduces the cleansing efficiency of soap.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds will decolourise bromine water?
questions.hint: Look for a compound containing a double bond.
questions.explanation: Ethene contains a carbon-carbon double bond and undergoes an addition reaction with bromine water, causing its colour to disappear.

questions.questionText: A compound X has the molecular formula C5H12. Which statement is correct?
questions.optionD: It contains a carbon-carbon double bond.
questions.hint: Apply the general formula of alkanes.
questions.explanation: C5H12 satisfies the general formula CnH2n+2. Therefore, it is pentane, a saturated hydrocarbon belonging to the alkane series.

questions.questionText: A student tests four compounds using bromine water. Compound P (C2H6), Q (C2H4), R (C3H8) and S (C4H10). Which compound will decolourise bromine water?
questions.hint: Only unsaturated hydrocarbons give this test.
questions.explanation: Among the given compounds, only C2H4 (ethene) is an unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon double bond. Therefore, only compound Q decolourises bromine water.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an allotrope of carbon?
questions.hint: Think of the hardest naturally occurring substance.
questions.explanation: Diamond is an allotrope of carbon. In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four other carbon atoms, making it extremely hard.

questions.questionText: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2OH is:
questions.hint: Count the number of carbon atoms and identify the functional group.
questions.explanation: CH3CH2OH contains two carbon atoms and a hydroxyl (-OH) group. Therefore, its IUPAC name is ethanol.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds belongs to the alkyne homologous series?
questions.hint: Use the general formula of alkynes.
questions.explanation: Alkynes have the general formula CnH2n-2. C2H2 (ethyne) satisfies this formula and contains a carbon-carbon triple bond.

questions.questionText: What is the product formed when ethanol is oxidised using alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate?
questions.hint: Oxidation increases the oxygen content of the compound.
questions.explanation: On oxidation, ethanol is converted into ethanoic acid. Oxidising agents such as alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7 are commonly used for this conversion.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct regarding detergents?
questions.optionA: They are ineffective in hard water.
questions.optionB: They form insoluble scum with calcium ions.
questions.optionC: They clean effectively in both hard and soft water.
questions.hint: Compare detergents with soaps.
questions.explanation: Detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with calcium or magnesium ions. Therefore, they remain effective in both hard and soft water.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds contains the aldehyde functional group?
questions.hint: Look for the -CHO functional group.
questions.explanation: CH3CHO is ethanal and contains the aldehyde (-CHO) functional group. The other compounds belong to different functional groups.

questions.questionText: During complete combustion of ethanol, the products formed are:
questions.hint: Complete combustion occurs in excess oxygen.
questions.explanation: Ethanol burns completely in excess oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water along with heat. The balanced equation is: C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O.

questions.questionText: A compound X has the molecular formula C4H10. Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.optionA: It contains a carbon-carbon double bond.
questions.optionB: It belongs to the alkane homologous series.
questions.hint: Compare the formula with the general formula of alkanes.
questions.explanation: C4H10 follows the general formula CnH2n+2. Therefore, it is butane, a saturated hydrocarbon belonging to the alkane series.

questions.questionText: A student has four compounds: P (C3H8), Q (C3H6), R (C3H4) and S (C3H7OH). Which compound definitely belongs to the alkene homologous series?
questions.hint: Use the general formula CnH2n.
questions.explanation: Alkenes follow the general formula CnH2n. C3H6 satisfies this formula and represents propene. The other compounds belong to different homologous series.

questions.questionText: A compound X reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate solution producing brisk effervescence. X also reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form a sweet-smelling substance. X is most likely:
questions.hint: Think about compounds that react with baking soda and undergo esterification.
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate to produce carbon dioxide gas. It also reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form the ester ethyl ethanoate, which has a pleasant fruity smell.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds is a member of the alkane homologous series?
questions.hint: Use the general formula of alkanes.
questions.explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2. C4H10 satisfies this formula and is butane, a saturated hydrocarbon.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the functional group of ketones?
questions.hint: It contains a carbonyl group between two carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: Ketones contain the carbonyl (>C=O) functional group attached to two carbon atoms. An example is propanone (CH3COCH3).

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Carbon forms compounds with long chains and ring structures. Reason (R): Carbon shows the property of catenation.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Recall the special property of carbon atoms bonding with one another.
questions.explanation: Carbon exhibits catenation, which allows carbon atoms to bond with one another to form long chains, branched chains and rings. Hence, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water. Reason (R): They undergo addition reactions due to the presence of double or triple bonds.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Think about the bromine water test.
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain double or triple bonds and undergo addition reactions with bromine, causing bromine water to lose its colour. Therefore, both statements are true and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs belong to the same homologous series?
questions.hint: Members of the same homologous series have the same functional group and general formula.
questions.explanation: CH4 (methane) and C2H6 (ethane) are both alkanes and belong to the same homologous series.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Soap molecules form micelles in water. Reason (R): The hydrophobic end of soap dissolves in water while the hydrophilic end dissolves in grease.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Recall which part of soap is attracted to water.
questions.explanation: Soap molecules form micelles in water, but the reason is incorrect because the hydrophilic end dissolves in water and the hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail dissolves in grease. Hence, the assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.questionText: Which of the following reactions is an example of substitution reaction?
questions.hint: One atom replaces another in this reaction.
questions.explanation: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight, where a hydrogen atom is replaced by chlorine. This is a substitution reaction.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Diamond does not conduct electricity. Reason (R): Every carbon atom in diamond uses all four valence electrons in covalent bonding.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Think about the availability of free electrons.
questions.explanation: In diamond, each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds, leaving no free electrons for electrical conduction. Hence, both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: A compound X has the molecular formula C5H10. It decolourises bromine water and undergoes hydrogenation to form C5H12. X is:
questions.hint: Use both the molecular formula and the reaction with bromine water.
questions.explanation: C5H10 follows the general formula CnH2n for alkenes. It decolourises bromine water due to the presence of a double bond and forms pentane (C5H12) on hydrogenation.

questions.questionText: A student has four colourless liquids: ethanol, ethanoic acid, hexane and propene. One liquid turns blue litmus red and reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate to produce brisk effervescence. Which liquid is it?
questions.hint: Look for a carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is acidic, so it turns blue litmus red. It also reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate to produce carbon dioxide gas, causing brisk effervescence. The other compounds do not show both these properties.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a life process essential for obtaining energy from food?
questions.hint: Think about the process that releases energy from glucose.
questions.explanation: Respiration is the process by which food is broken down to release energy required for all activities of the body. Transportation and excretion are also life processes but do not directly release energy.

questions.questionText: The green pigment present in leaves that traps solar energy is called:
questions.hint: It is present inside chloroplasts.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment present in chloroplasts. It absorbs sunlight required for the process of photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: Which raw material for photosynthesis is absorbed from the atmosphere?
questions.hint: Plants take this gas through stomata.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere through stomata and is used along with water to prepare food during photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: Where does the complete breakdown of glucose occur during aerobic respiration?
questions.hint: It is known as the powerhouse of the cell.
questions.explanation: The complete oxidation of glucose during aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria, releasing carbon dioxide, water and a large amount of energy in the form of ATP.

questions.questionText: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.hint: It is an exception among veins.
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein carries oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. It is the only vein that carries oxygenated blood.

questions.questionText: Which component of blood is mainly responsible for transporting oxygen to body tissues?
questions.hint: It contains haemoglobin.
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds with oxygen in the lungs and transports it to different parts of the body.

questions.questionText: In plants, water and minerals are transported mainly through:
questions.hint: It conducts water from roots to leaves.
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant. Phloem transports food.

questions.questionText: Which part of the human nephron performs ultrafiltration of blood?
questions.hint: It is a network of capillaries inside Bowman's capsule.
questions.explanation: Ultrafiltration occurs in the glomerulus, where water, salts, glucose and nitrogenous wastes are filtered from the blood into Bowman's capsule.

questions.questionText: A plant is kept in the dark for two days and then exposed to sunlight for a few hours. After performing the iodine test on a leaf, a blue-black colour is observed. This indicates that:
questions.optionB: Starch has been formed due to photosynthesis.
questions.hint: Iodine solution is used to test for a stored food product.
questions.explanation: The blue-black colour with iodine confirms the presence of starch, showing that photosynthesis occurred in the presence of sunlight and produced glucose, which was stored as starch.

questions.questionText: A person suffers damage to the alveoli of the lungs due to prolonged smoking. Which process will be affected most directly?
questions.optionC: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide
questions.hint: Think about the primary function of alveoli.
questions.explanation: Alveoli provide a large surface area for the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between the air and blood. Damage to the alveoli reduces the efficiency of gaseous exchange and makes breathing difficult.

questions.questionText: Which gas is released as a by-product during photosynthesis?
questions.hint: It is essential for aerobic respiration.
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, plants prepare glucose using carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll. Oxygen is released as a by-product.

questions.questionText: The process by which food moves from the mouth to the stomach through the oesophagus is called:
questions.hint: It involves rhythmic muscular contractions.
questions.explanation: Peristalsis is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles in the alimentary canal that pushes food towards the stomach.

questions.questionText: Which enzyme present in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
questions.hint: It acts in the mouth.
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) breaks down starch into simpler sugars in the mouth, initiating carbohydrate digestion.

questions.questionText: Which chamber of the human heart has the thickest muscular wall?
questions.hint: It pumps blood to the entire body.
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it pumps oxygenated blood to all parts of the body at high pressure.

questions.questionText: Which tissue transports prepared food from leaves to other parts of the plant?
questions.hint: It transports sugars produced during photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Phloem transports food, mainly in the form of sucrose, from leaves to growing and storage regions of the plant. This process is called translocation.

questions.questionText: Which nitrogenous waste is mainly excreted by human kidneys?
questions.hint: It is produced in the liver from ammonia.
questions.explanation: Humans are ureotelic animals. The kidneys remove urea from the blood and eliminate it in urine.

questions.questionText: Which of the following helps in preventing the backflow of blood in the human heart?
questions.hint: These structures ensure one-way flow of blood.
questions.explanation: Valves in the heart prevent the backflow of blood and ensure that blood flows in only one direction through the chambers of the heart.

questions.questionText: During vigorous exercise, muscle cells may temporarily switch to anaerobic respiration. What is the end product formed in human muscles?
questions.hint: It causes muscle cramps when accumulated.
questions.explanation: During oxygen deficiency, muscle cells perform anaerobic respiration and produce lactic acid along with a small amount of energy. Accumulation of lactic acid may cause muscle cramps.

questions.questionText: A plant is watered regularly but its stomata remain closed due to very high temperature. Which process will be affected most directly?
questions.optionB: Photosynthesis due to reduced carbon dioxide intake
questions.hint: Think about the role of stomata in gas exchange.
questions.explanation: When stomata remain closed, carbon dioxide cannot enter the leaf efficiently. As a result, photosynthesis decreases even if water is available.

questions.questionText: A person's kidneys fail to filter blood effectively. Which medical procedure is commonly used to remove nitrogenous wastes from the blood until kidney function is restored or replaced?
questions.hint: It uses an artificial filtering system.
questions.explanation: Dialysis is a medical procedure in which an artificial kidney (dialysis machine) removes urea, excess salts and water from the blood when the kidneys cannot perform this function adequately.

questions.questionText: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium of the heart?
questions.hint: It is the largest vein in the body.
questions.explanation: The superior and inferior vena cava bring deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body to the right atrium.

questions.questionText: Which part of the digestive system secretes hydrochloric acid?
questions.hint: It helps activate pepsin.
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is secreted by the gastric glands of the stomach. It creates an acidic medium for the action of pepsin and kills harmful microorganisms.

questions.questionText: Which pigment present in red blood cells transports oxygen?
questions.hint: It contains iron.
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin is an iron-containing respiratory pigment present in red blood cells. It binds with oxygen in the lungs and transports it throughout the body.

questions.questionText: Which event takes place in the alveoli of the lungs?
questions.optionC: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide
questions.hint: Think about the function of alveoli.
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs where oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out of the blood for exhalation.

questions.questionText: Which process is responsible for the upward movement of water through the xylem in plants?
questions.hint: Water loss from leaves creates a pulling force.
questions.explanation: Transpiration creates a suction force called transpiration pull, which helps move water and dissolved minerals upward through the xylem.

questions.questionText: Which organ produces bile that helps in the digestion of fats?
questions.hint: The bile is stored in the gall bladder.
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, which emulsifies fats into small droplets, making their digestion easier. The bile is stored temporarily in the gall bladder.

questions.questionText: Which structure in the nephron is mainly responsible for selective reabsorption of useful substances?
questions.hint: Useful substances are taken back into the blood after filtration.
questions.explanation: Selective reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, salts and water mainly occurs in the renal tubule before urine is formed.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes double circulation in humans?
questions.optionA: Blood passes through the heart only once in one complete cycle.
questions.optionB: Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix completely.
questions.optionC: Blood passes through the heart twice in one complete cycle, preventing mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
questions.hint: Think about pulmonary and systemic circulation.
questions.explanation: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice during one complete cycle—once through pulmonary circulation and once through systemic circulation. This ensures efficient oxygen transport by preventing mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

questions.questionText: A person has a reduced number of red blood cells. Which process is likely to be affected first?
questions.optionA: Transport of oxygen to body tissues
questions.hint: Consider the function of haemoglobin.
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which transports oxygen. A decrease in their number reduces oxygen supply to body tissues, leading to fatigue and weakness.

questions.questionText: A student places one healthy potted plant in sunlight and another identical plant in a sealed container without carbon dioxide. After a few hours, both leaves are tested with iodine solution. Which observation is most likely?
questions.optionC: Only the leaf from the plant in sunlight with carbon dioxide turns blue-black.
questions.optionD: Only the leaf from the sealed container turns blue-black.
questions.hint: Carbon dioxide is an essential raw material for photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide, water, chlorophyll and sunlight. The plant kept without carbon dioxide cannot synthesize glucose, so starch is not formed. Therefore, only the leaf from the plant receiving both sunlight and carbon dioxide gives a blue-black colour with iodine.

questions.questionText: Which process is responsible for the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant?
questions.hint: This process mainly occurs through stomata.
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of plants, mainly through stomata. It also helps in cooling the plant and creating transpiration pull.

questions.questionText: Which chamber of the human heart receives oxygenated blood from the lungs?
questions.hint: Blood enters this chamber through the pulmonary veins.
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium, from where it passes into the left ventricle.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): The small intestine is the main site of absorption of digested food. Reason (R): The inner lining of the small intestine has numerous villi that increase the surface area for absorption.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Think about the role of villi.
questions.explanation: The small intestine contains numerous finger-like projections called villi that greatly increase the surface area for absorption of digested nutrients. Therefore, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to leaves. Reason (R): Xylem consists mainly of dead cells that form continuous tubes.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Recall the structure and function of xylem.
questions.explanation: Xylem is composed mainly of dead vessel elements and tracheids that form continuous tubes for efficient transport of water and minerals. Hence, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Which structure prevents food from entering the windpipe during swallowing?
questions.hint: It acts like a flap over the windpipe.
questions.explanation: The epiglottis closes the opening of the trachea during swallowing, preventing food from entering the windpipe.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Anaerobic respiration releases less energy than aerobic respiration. Reason (R): Glucose is only partially broken down during anaerobic respiration.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Compare the breakdown of glucose in both types of respiration.
questions.explanation: In anaerobic respiration, glucose is incompletely broken down into lactic acid (in muscles) or ethanol and carbon dioxide (in yeast), releasing much less energy than aerobic respiration. Thus, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: Which part of the nephron is primarily responsible for collecting the final urine before it passes into the ureter?
questions.hint: It receives fluid from several nephrons.
questions.explanation: The collecting duct receives urine from many nephrons and carries it towards the renal pelvis before it enters the ureter.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood. Reason (R): All arteries carry oxygenated blood.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionC: A is false, but R is true.
questions.optionD: Both A and R are false.
questions.hint: Remember the exception among arteries.
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery is an exception because it carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. Therefore, the assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.questionText: A patient has a blockage in the coronary arteries supplying the heart muscles. Which process will be affected most directly?
questions.optionB: Supply of oxygen to the heart muscles
questions.hint: Think about the function of coronary arteries.
questions.explanation: Coronary arteries supply oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscles. A blockage reduces oxygen supply, which may lead to a heart attack.

questions.questionText: A plant is kept under bright sunlight but is not watered for several days. The stomata close to reduce water loss. Which process will decrease first due to stomatal closure?
questions.optionB: Photosynthesis due to reduced carbon dioxide entry
questions.hint: Stomata are involved in gas exchange.
questions.explanation: Closing of stomata reduces the entry of carbon dioxide into the leaves. Since carbon dioxide is an essential raw material for photosynthesis, the rate of photosynthesis decreases first, even in bright sunlight.

questions.questionText: Which part of the neuron receives information from receptors or other neurons?
questions.hint: It consists of short, branched projections.
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive nerve impulses from receptors or other neurons and transmit them towards the cell body. The axon carries impulses away from the cell body.

questions.questionText: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is:
questions.hint: It is also called a nerve cell.
questions.explanation: A neuron is the basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system. It receives, processes and transmits nerve impulses.

questions.questionText: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for maintaining posture and balance of the body?
questions.hint: It coordinates muscular activity.
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary muscle movements and maintains posture, precision and balance of the body.

questions.questionText: Reflex actions are mainly controlled by the:
questions.hint: It enables a quick response without conscious thinking.
questions.explanation: Reflex actions are rapid, automatic responses controlled mainly by the spinal cord. The brain is informed after the response has already occurred.

questions.questionText: Which hormone helps regulate the level of sugar in human blood?
questions.hint: It is secreted by the pancreas.
questions.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas and helps lower blood glucose by promoting its uptake by cells and conversion into glycogen.

questions.questionText: Which plant hormone promotes cell elongation and bending of shoots towards light?
questions.hint: It is mainly produced in shoot tips.
questions.explanation: Auxin promotes cell elongation. During phototropism, auxin accumulates on the shaded side of the stem, causing greater elongation and bending towards light.

questions.questionText: A student accidentally touches a hot pan and immediately withdraws the hand. Which sequence correctly represents the reflex arc?
questions.optionA: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Spinal cord → Motor neuron → Effector
questions.optionB: Receptor → Motor neuron → Brain → Sensory neuron → Muscle
questions.optionC: Brain → Sensory neuron → Motor neuron → Receptor
questions.hint: The response is coordinated without involving the brain first.
questions.explanation: In a reflex arc, receptors detect the stimulus. Sensory neurons carry the impulse to a relay neuron in the spinal cord, which passes it to a motor neuron. The motor neuron carries the impulse to an effector (muscle or gland), producing a rapid response.

questions.questionText: Which endocrine gland is called the 'master gland' because it controls the activity of several other endocrine glands?
questions.hint: It is located at the base of the brain.
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland secretes hormones that regulate the activity of several other endocrine glands. Therefore, it is called the master gland.

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Adrenaline prepares the body for emergency situations. Reason (R): It increases heart rate, breathing rate and blood flow to muscles.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.optionC: A is true, but R is false.
questions.optionD: A is false, but R is true.
questions.hint: Think about the 'fight or flight' response.
questions.explanation: Adrenaline is secreted during stressful situations. It increases heart rate, breathing rate and blood supply to muscles, preparing the body for quick action. Hence, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.questionText: A potted plant is placed horizontally near a window through which sunlight enters. After two days, the shoot bends upward towards the light while the root grows downward. Which combination of tropic responses is shown?
questions.optionA: Positive phototropism in shoot and positive geotropism in root
questions.optionB: Negative phototropism in shoot and positive geotropism in root
questions.optionC: Positive phototropism in both shoot and root
questions.optionD: Negative geotropism in root and positive phototropism in shoot
questions.hint: Shoots respond mainly to light, whereas roots respond mainly to gravity.
questions.explanation: Shoots exhibit positive phototropism by growing towards light. Roots exhibit positive geotropism by growing in the direction of gravity. These responses help the plant maximize photosynthesis and water absorption.

questions.questionText: Which part of the human brain controls voluntary actions such as writing and speaking?
questions.hint: It is the largest part of the brain.
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for voluntary actions, thinking, memory, intelligence and interpretation of sensory information.

questions.questionText: Which hormone is secreted by the thyroid gland?
questions.hint: Its production requires iodine.
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxine, which regulates metabolism, growth and development. Iodine is essential for its synthesis.

questions.questionText: Which receptor helps us detect light?
questions.hint: It is present in the retina of the eye.
questions.explanation: Photoreceptors present in the retina detect light and convert it into nerve impulses that are interpreted by the brain.

questions.questionText: Which hormone is responsible for the 'fight or flight' response?
questions.hint: It is secreted by the adrenal glands.
questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body to respond quickly during emergencies by increasing heart rate, breathing rate and blood flow to muscles.

questions.questionText: Which plant hormone promotes cell division?
questions.hint: It is active in growing tissues.
questions.explanation: Cytokinins stimulate cell division and help in the growth of plant tissues. They also delay ageing in leaves.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a reflex action?
questions.optionC: Blinking when dust enters the eye
questions.hint: It is an automatic protective response.
questions.explanation: Blinking when dust enters the eye is an involuntary, rapid response that protects the eye. It is a reflex action.

questions.questionText: Which hormone deficiency causes diabetes mellitus?
questions.hint: It regulates blood glucose level.
